structure: Part 15 of trace:e2e: the INS project. Read in full the ten spec files under repos/trade-imports-ins-tests/tests/ins/e2e/features (address-book-add-handshake-guard, address-book-auth, address-book-cross-user-visibility, address-book-delete, address-book-edit, address-book-persistence, address-book, aggregated-notification, cross-service-sessions, notification-dashboard-navigation) and mined all 13 trace zips, every one passed. The `tim distil trace ... -- open` command refuses these zips (TraceVersionError: the trace was created by a newer Playwright than the viewer tim installs), so each zip was mined from its unpacked copy already in this part's working folder (part15/<hash>/, checked against `unzip -l` of the zip: same entries and byte sizes), reading actions from <n>-trace.trace, rendered DOM from the frame snapshots and the network log from <n>-trace.network with jq. Refs name a trace by its hash: 6aeac = refuses an unrecognised journey type; bf1ec = lands on the sign in page past the landing page; 98ed4 = allows signing into a page past the landing page; 1e792 = an address added by one user is visible to another; 83967 = deleting tombstones the record; f92fd = an address deleted by one user is gone for another; 31c45 = an edit replaces the whole record; ee957 = the edited address replaces the old one; 54e97 = a created address persists with its full Standard Address Block; 3c6f9 = renders the address book after signing in; 28659 = aggregated notification through the submission lifecycle; 3157d = animals, then ins, then plants keeps all three sessions; 1de58 = INS dashboard View opens the owning journey frontend. Each ref is `trace <hash> action <call id>` (a snapshot taken at that action) or `trace <hash> request <method> <path>`, or a spec file and line. Page inventory, in the order a user meets it: (1) Defra ID stub sign-in (Sign in using Government Gateway), then (2) Choose your organisation only for a user with more than one organisation; (3) INS address book landing page /address-book (always after sign-in); (4) Add address details /address-book/add; (5) Edit address details /address-book/{id}/edit; (6) Delete address /address-book/{id}/delete; each of 4-6 returns to (3) with a success banner; (7) the 404 Page not found page for an add handshake with an unknown journey type; (8) INS Dashboard / with search, sort, table and View link; (9) the animals and plants dashboards, reached only as session checks; (10) the animals journey from Start a new notification to Import notification submitted (28659 and 1de58, used as set-up for the aggregate and the dashboard hand-off; its pages are recorded only where they bear on INS); (11) the animals Review your notification read-only view at /notification-view, reached from the INS dashboard. Not reached by any trace: the address detail page /address-book/{id}, address-book search results, page 2 of either list, every validation error on add and edit, every Cancel button, a recognised add handshake, sign-out, and an organisation that should not see another's addresses; these are recorded as gaps. The aggregated notification's stored fields come from the spec's Mongo assertions (the browser trace cannot show Mongo), which held because the test passed.

claims.statement: Deleting is a tombstone, not a removal: fetching the address by id afterwards still returns it, with its name intact and deleted set to true.
Tombstoned addresses are left out of the address book list and search; only the by-id lookup returns them, so a notification that references a deleted address does not dangle.
claims.quote: The record is still there, flagged — the by-id endpoint is the only way to see it, because list and search both omit tombstones. A hard delete would 404 here and leave any notification referencing it dangling.
claims.note: The list omission is shown in the trace (call@88); the search omission is stated by the spec only, since no trace searches.

claims.statement: The address book belongs to the organisation, not the user: an address one user adds is listed for another user signed in to the same organisation.

claims.statement: An address one user deletes is gone from the address book of another user in the same organisation.
No trace shows a user in a different organisation, so it is not evidenced that one organisation cannot see another's addresses.

The address book API is scoped by organisation in its path: POST /organisation/{organisationId}/addresses creates an address (201, Location /organisation/{organisationId}/addresses/{id}), sent with an x-api-key header and a Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header.
claims.note: x-api-key value [REDACTED]. The call is made by the test fixture directly; the INS frontend's own calls to this API are server-side and not in the trace.

claims.statement: GET /organisation/{organisationId}/addresses/{id} returns one address, including a tombstoned one.
A stored address (the Standard Address Block) holds id, name, addressLine1, addressLine2, townOrCity, county, postcode, countryCode, phone, email, organisationId, deleted, createdAt and modifiedAt.

Addresses created through the API under organisation id 5900001 appear in the INS address book of users signed in to Gatwick Airport (SBI 110100101), so INS maps the signed-in organisation to address-book organisation 5900001.
claims.ref: trace 83967 request POST /organisation/5900001/addresses; trace f92fd action call@78; trace 3c6f9 action call@62
claims.note: How the SBI chosen at sign-in becomes organisation id 5900001 is not visible in the trace.

claims.statement: The INS frontend's own calls to the address book API (list, create, update, delete) happen server-side and none appears in the browser trace.

The aggregated notification trace builds a live-animals notification through the animals journey (origin, commodity, commodity details, identification, reason for import, additional details, five consignment addresses, CPH number, arrival details, transit countries, transporter, contact address, review, declaration) and submits it as GBN-AG-26-BGJNRA.
claims.note: The journey's pages are set-up for the INS assertions; they are recorded in full by the animals parts of this source.

claims.statement: Submitting shows a confirmation panel Import notification submitted with Your reference number and the reference.
claims.quote: Import notification submitted / Your reference number GBN-AG-26-BGJNRA

claims.statement: The confirmation page then lists next steps under Before the consignment is imported, Transporting the consignment, How to view or amend this notification (with Return to your dashboard and Create a new notification) and Getting help.
claims.quote: Before the consignment is imported / You still need to: upload the health certificate and any other required documents / Transporting the consignment / How to view or amend this notification / You can view or amend this notification from your dashboard and resubmit it. / Return to your dashboard / Create a new notification / Getting help

claims.statement: INS keeps one aggregated read-model document per notification in the trade-imports-ins-backend notifications collection, with the id Imports.Notification.GBN-AG.<reference number>.
claims.note: Asserted against Mongo by the spec; the test passed in trace 28659.

claims.statement: The aggregated document exists as soon as the notification is created (a NOTIFICATION_CREATED event fires at creation, before transport details are filled in), with status DRAFT.
claims.quote: NOTIFICATION_CREATED fires immediately at creation (before transport details are filled in), so we poll for the specific fully-populated state rather than bare status=DRAFT.

claims.statement: Before submission the aggregated document reflects the edited draft: status DRAFT, the reference number, origin country, commodity Cow, an arrival date in the future, a lastUpdated date and an aggregateVersion above 0.
claims.note: The journey posted countryOfOrigin=FR and arrivalDateAtPort=7/11/2026 (trace 28659), so originCountry is the country code.

claims.statement: The aggregated document's commodity is the common name Cow, resolved from the Bos taurus species the user picked.
Submitting updates the same aggregated document to SUBMITTED rather than creating a second one: exactly one document exists for the notification.
claims.quote: Then — same document is updated to SUBMITTED (no duplicate created) ... expect(await collection.countDocuments({ _id: aggregateId })).toBe(1);

claims.statement: After submission the aggregated document keeps the reference, origin country, commodity, future arrival date and a lastUpdated date, and its aggregateVersion is higher than the draft's.
The aggregated store is updated asynchronously from journey events: it catches up with the journey some time after each change rather than in the same request.
claims.quote: await expect.poll(() => collection.findOne({ _id: aggregateId, status: 'SUBMITTED' }), { timeout: timeouts.long }).not.toBeNull();
claims.note: The spec has to poll with a long timeout, and the INS dashboard still showed DRAFT for three searches after submission (claim trace-e2e-p15-106).
